info.title: Hermoso API
info.summary: Publish, schedule and manage social content from your own backend.
info.x-guidance: Hermoso makes, posts and runs marketing for a brand. An agent with its own payment credential (MPP, e.g. a Stripe Shared Payment Token) signs up with POST /api/signup/machine-payment and a JSON body {email, claim_token, plan or packId}: it answers 402 with a challenge for exactly that plan month or credit pack; pay it and retry the same body to receive an hmk_ API key. With a key, POST /api/billing/machine-payment (key in X-Api-Key) buys more credits or a plan month the same way, and every /v1 endpoint takes Authorization: Bearer hmk_... (GET /v1/tools lists everything callable). Prices and ids: GET /api/billing/config, under machinePayments.
info.description:
The Hermoso public API. Server-side only — it sends no CORS headers and cannot be called from browser JavaScript, because an API key carries full account authority and a key shipped to a browser is a key you have published. The one exception is Hermoso’s own apps inside Canva, Adobe Express and Figma, where a person signs in to their own account and the token is theirs (lib/editor-apps-cors.mjs).

Start free: 160+ free credits, no card. No markup on models.

## Compatibility

ADD FREELY, NEVER BREAK. Inside `/v1` we add endpoints, optional request fields and response fields without notice, and enums grow — a new publishing channel is an addition, not a version. We never remove a field, change its type or meaning, change a default, or change the status code of an existing condition. Anything that cannot obey that gets a `/v2`, and `/v1` then keeps serving for at least 12 months carrying `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers (RFC 8594).

So: **ignore fields you do not recognise, and tolerate enum values you have not seen.** Those two habits are what make the promise worth anything.

The `/api/*` routes this app uses internally are NOT part of any contract. They change without notice and are not documented here. Do not call them. **Two exceptions, both listed in `paths` below:** `POST /api/billing/machine-payment` (a key-holding account buys credits or a prepaid plan month) and `POST /api/signup/machine-payment` (an agent with no account signs up and pays in one call). The Machine Payments Protocol discovers a payable endpoint by reading `x-payment-info` out of an OpenAPI document, so an endpoint that is not in this document cannot be found by a wallet at all. They are not in `/v1` because a `402` challenge has to be a raw response carrying `WWW-Authenticate`, and every `/v1` handler returns an object this API wraps in its own envelope. Treat those two paths as covered by the same never-break promise as `/v1`.

## Two tiers, both first-class

`/v1/tools` is FULL PARITY with the Hermoso toolset, and it EVOLVES WITH IT. Two different promises live in this API, and it is worth knowing which one you are standing on.

**The modelled resources** — `/v1/posts`, `/v1/channels`, `/v1/media`, `/v1/credits` — obey the compatibility promise above in full. Add freely, never break. Build a product on them.

**The tool passthrough** — `/v1/tools` and `/v1/tools/{name}` — reaches everything else Hermoso does: research, generation, publishing, paid campaigns on every connected ad platform, analytics, files, workspace. Its ENVELOPE is stable under the same promise: the routes, the authentication, the error shape, the rate-limit headers, the idempotency semantics and this document. THE TOOLS INSIDE IT ARE NOT FROZEN — their arguments and results improve as the tools do, continuously and without a version bump.

So read the roster rather than pinning it: `GET /v1/tools` is a live read, filterable by area and searchable, and `GET /v1/tools/{name}` is the current schema for one tool. Neither tier is the lesser door — pick per job.

## Authentication

`Authorization: Bearer hmk_...`. Create a key in the app (https://app.hermoso.ai) on the API, MCP & CLI tab, under Terminal & API keys. Keys are hashed at rest and revocable, and one key can never mint another.

A key is created with two choices: what it reaches, and the access it has.

REACH is the whole account or ONE brand. A whole-account key can act on every brand the account holds. A key limited to one brand acts inside that brand only: `GET /v1/brands` lists that one brand, any other `X-Hermoso-User` (or brand named on a call) is refused with a 403 whose `error.code` is `brand_key_scope`, and creating or deleting brands, account settings and the account’s contact email are refused the same way.

ACCESS is member or admin. A member key does the work (research, creation, scheduling, posting, ads) and reads the credit balance and plan. It cannot manage the team, change billing, create or delete brands, or change account settings: those are refused with a 403 whose message begins “This key has member access.” (`error.code` `key_member_access`). An admin key can also manage the team (a one-brand admin key: that brand’s team) and make the billing changes this API offers. Billing belongs to the account, whichever brand a key is limited to. A key created with no access named is admin when it reaches the whole account and member when it is limited to one brand. A key never has more rights than the person who created it.

No key, of either reach or access, can list, create or revoke keys. Every key can read the credit balance and plan with `GET /v1/credits`, because credits belong to the account. Deleting a brand revokes the keys limited to it.

A third-party app acting on behalf of a Hermoso user runs the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with PKCE (`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`; dynamic client registration is supported). That flow MINTS one of these same keys, so there is one credential type and one set of guarantees, not two. One connection grants everything the account can do — there is no scope selection to negotiate.

## Workspaces

An account can hold several profiles, and `GET /v1/brands` lists them. A whole-account key is pinned to one, and `X-Hermoso-User: <profile-id>` overrides it per request (a key limited to one brand has no other profile to name). An id this key cannot act on is refused with a 404 `brand_not_found` rather than answered with empty results. The workspace is NEVER read from a request body. Membership is re-authorised on every single request, so a body field naming a workspace is refused rather than honoured.

## Long-running work

A render takes longer than a request should. By default `POST /v1/tools/{name}` holds a render for up to 45 seconds and then hands back a job id inside a 200. Send `?wait=0` and it answers 202 with a job handle the moment the job is queued; poll `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` until `status` is `done` or `error`. Not waiting changes nothing about what the render costs. Never re-call the tool to check on a render: that starts a second one.

## Rate limits

Per API key: 300 reads and 60 writes per minute. Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; a 429 also carries `Retry-After`. Two keys on one account get two independent budgets.

bearerAuth.description: A Hermoso API key, or an access token from the OAuth authorization-code flow (which is the same thing).

apiKeyHeader.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyHeader.description: A Hermoso API key (hmk_...) in X-Api-Key. Accepted only when Authorization is absent or carries an MPP `Payment` credential: the machine-payment retry needs Authorization for the payment.

type.description: The coarse family — branch on this. New CODES land inside an existing type wherever possible so that branch keeps working; the enum is published for code generation, and a client should still fall through gracefully on a member it does not recognise.

code.description: The specific reason. Log this. New values may appear at any time.

param.description: The offending field, when there is one.

connector.description: Present when the reason is a channel that is not connected. Reconnect in the app — an OAuth consent screen cannot be completed headlessly.

credits_needed.description: On `insufficient_credits` from a recast or an edit: what the request needs.

balance.description: On `insufficient_credits` from a recast or an edit: what this workspace has.

did_you_mean.description: An argument THIS tool declares that the key most likely meant, or null.

unknown_arguments.description: On `invalid_arguments` from POST /v1/tools/{name}: each key the tool does not take, with the argument it most likely meant. Nothing was run.

upgrade_url.description: On `real_face_needs_paid`: where to choose a paid plan.

alternative.description: On `real_face_needs_paid`: the field that works on every plan instead (`person.describe`).

person_url.description: On a recast with `person.describe` whose recast step was refused after the person was made: the AI person, in your Library. Send it as `person.image_url` to retry without making a new one.

warnings.description: Present when the request also carried a parameter or field this operation does not take. Often the reason for the error (a misnamed field reads as a missing one).

status.description: scheduled | processing | published | partially_published | failed | indeterminate. THIS SET MAY GROW — tolerate an unknown value. `indeterminate` means a restart interrupted the send and we cannot say whether it published: check the channel rather than assuming either way. `failed` is only ever used when we know nothing published.

title_effective.description: The headline actually going out — derived from the caption when you named none.

targets.description: Which account this goes to, per channel (Page, board, LinkedIn Page, Business listing). Unset means the connection’s default.

results.description: Per-channel outcome once fired. A partial failure is normal and is reported here — the top-level status then says `partially_published`, never a flat `failed`.

first_comment.description: Present when the post carried `first_comment`. `posted` true with the comment `id`, or false with `note` saying why (`skipped` when the channel takes no first comment, or it was already posted by an earlier run). A failed comment never fails the channel.

status_detail.description: Present when the status alone would mislead. Set for `indeterminate`.

channels.description: One or more channel ids from GET /v1/channels. DELIBERATELY NOT AN ENUM — the set is derived from what the product can publish to, and it GROWS as platform approvals land. Read it from GET /v1/channels rather than hard-coding it, and treat an id you have not seen as valid.

caption.description: The post text. Per-channel length limits are enforced at create time, not discovered at publish time.

title.description: The headline Pinterest and YouTube each require. Derived from the caption when omitted.

media.description: Ordered. One item is a single post; two or more are a carousel, in the order given. Each item is a Hermoso-hosted URL from POST /v1/media, as a bare string or as {url, type}.

scheduled_at.description: Omit to publish immediately. Otherwise ISO-8601, at least 60 seconds out and within the documented horizon.

use_queue.description: Take the next free slot in this profile’s posting schedule instead of naming a time. Mutually exclusive with scheduled_at — sending both is an error, never a silent precedence.

timezone.description: IANA zone for use_queue. Defaults to the profile’s saved zone.

visibility.description: public (default) | unlisted | private | draft. Refused at create time where a channel cannot honour it, never silently downgraded at publish time.

captions_by_channel.description: Override the caption for one channel.

targets.description: Which account to post to, where the connection holds more than one. Omit for the default. GET /v1/channels names the field each channel uses.

options.description: Per-channel publish metadata (YouTube description, tags, categoryId, madeForKids, notifySubscribers, paidProductPlacement, brandPartner and a captionTrack {url|text, language, name} uploaded right after the video; X thread parts, Instagram alt text, and so on).

labels.description: Your own labels for finding the post again (up to 10, 40 characters each). Never published. GET /v1/posts?label= filters on them.

external_id.description: Your own id for the post (up to 128 characters), e.g. a CRM or sheet row id. GET /v1/posts?external_id= finds it, also after it publishes.

metadata.description: Your own key/value notes stored with the post: strings, numbers, booleans or null, up to 20 keys and 4 KB. Refused, never trimmed, when over.

dry_run.description: Run every check a create runs and store nothing. Answers 200 with {ok, channels, media, pipeline, note}: lengths per channel (with X’s weighted count), each media URL identified and measured from its bytes, and the exact refusal a create would get.

first_comment.description: A comment the account posts on its own post right after it publishes: Facebook Pages, Instagram, and LinkedIn company Pages (LinkedIn needs its comments authorization, provider linkedin_community). Up to 2,000 characters, refused (never cut) when longer. Other channels publish the post without it and say so on their result. A comment that fails never undoes the post; its outcome is reported on the channel’s result.

PostUpdate.description: Any subset of PostCreate. Omitted means unchanged; an explicit empty value clears.

connector.description: The connection this channel is reached through. Several channels can share one — Facebook and Instagram both ride the Meta connection.

available.description: Whether this channel can be connected AT ALL on this deployment. False while a platform approval is outstanding — a different answer from "you have not connected it yet", and collapsing the two would send you to build a connect flow that cannot succeed.

needs_reconnect.description: A row exists but holds no usable credential. Reconnect in the app, or send the account holder a link from POST /v1/connect-links.

account.description: Which account is connected, where the provider tells us.

max.description: The vendor’s own cap. null means the vendor publishes no number — render that as "no documented limit", never as unlimited and never as an invented cap.

target_field.description: The key inside `targets` that names WHICH account on this channel to post to.

url.description: A durable Hermoso-hosted URL. Pass it straight into POST /v1/posts.

balance.description: Hermoso credits available to this workspace.

shared_workspace.description: True when this key is acting inside a workspace owned by another account — the balance is then the owner’s pool, which is what your renders spend.

limits.description: The monthly credit limits on the brand this key acts on (or the brand named by `?brand=`). The account owner can cap what a brand, or one member of a shared brand, spends in a UTC calendar month; when one would be passed, paid calls answer `429` with `error.code` `credit_limit` (and `Retry-After` until the reset). `limit: null` means no limit. Null here (with `limits_error`) means the read failed, never that there are no limits.

month.description: The UTC calendar month the usage covers, `YYYY-MM`.

reset_at.description: When every limit’s month resets (00:00 UTC on the 1st).

can_edit.description: True only for the account owner. Set a limit with the `set_credit_limit` tool (`POST /v1/tools/set_credit_limit`).

held.description: Credits held for work still running, which count against the limit.

members.description: Present for the owner and a brand admin (a member sees only their own row).

limits_error.description: Present only when the limits could not be read.

plan.description: A PAID plan id — see GET /v1/signup/plans-equivalent on hermoso.ai/pricing, currently starter, pro or studio. The free plan is refused here by name: this path provisions an account only against a completed payment.

email.description: REQUIRED: a real mailbox for the human this account belongs to. A verification link is emailed there; the account works before it is clicked, and verifying only decides whether we may mail the address (receipts, low-credit alerts, replies to bug reports). It is NEVER the account identity: it cannot sign in to this account, and it can never link or merge this account with one that already uses the address. Hermoso synthetic addresses are refused (400 `email_invalid`).

claim_token.description: The token returned exactly once by POST /v1/signup.

area.description: Which area of the product it belongs to. THIS SET MAY GROW — tolerate a member you have not seen.

description.description: What it does, written for whoever is choosing: a person reading the index or a model reading the roster.

read_only.description: It reads and changes nothing. Read-only tools are metered on the READ rate-limit budget.

destructive.description: It can remove or overwrite something. Destructive tools carry their own confirmation arguments — read the schema.

idempotent.description: Calling it twice with the same arguments has the same effect as calling it once. Independent of `Idempotency-Key`, which protects a retry regardless.

requires_connector.description: The third-party account this tool needs linked, or null when it needs none. Linking is a browser flow: an OAuth consent screen cannot be completed headlessly.

connector_connected.description: Whether that connector is linked in this workspace. NULL means the connections could not be read, which is NOT the same as "no" — never render it as a refusal.

rate_class.description: Which rate-limit budget a call to it spends.

price.description: What one call spends, in credits, before you run it: "free", a range by model for a raw generation tool ("0.4-32.5 credits by model and size"), "from N credits" for one that scales with length or work, or "credits vary: get_cost prices it". Every number is read live from the model catalog; send `get_cost: true` to a paying tool for the exact quote. NULL means it was not priced on this read.

available.description: Only with `include=all`: whether this workspace can call it right now (false on a tool that needs something first, see `unavailable_reason`). Absent from the default index, every row of which is callable.

unavailable_reason.description: Only with `include=all`. `not_connected` (link `requires_connector`, at `connect_url`), `not_offered` (the platform is not offered on this server yet, so there is nothing to link) or `shopify_store` (it needs a Shopify store on the account). Null when `available` is true. THIS SET MAY GROW.

connect_url.description: Only with `include=all`, and only on a `not_connected` row: the link a person opens to connect `requires_connector` to this brand. To have your own customer connect their account from your app, use POST /v1/connect-links instead.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for the request body of POST /v1/tools/{name}. The body IS the argument object.

areas.description: Every area holding at least one tool available to this workspace, so one call shows the whole map before you page through it.

total.description: Tools matching this filter, across all pages.

ranked.description: True: rows are in relevance order. False only if the ranking was unavailable on this server, in which case rows are a plain text match in roster order.

strong_matches.description: How many of the top rows match strongly (a word of the query is in the tool’s name). The rows after them are looser matches.

Warning.description: Something about the request that did not stop it but probably did not do what you meant. Today: a query parameter or body field this operation does not take, which was IGNORED. Any response, success or error, may carry `warnings`; read it in development and fix what it names. THIS SET OF CODES MAY GROW.

code.description: `unknown_parameter` (a query parameter) or `unknown_field` (a JSON body field).

did_you_mean.description: The parameter of THIS operation you most likely meant.

valid.description: Every name this operation takes there.

ToolCall.description: The TOOL’S OWN arguments, as a flat object. There is no wrapper: to call a tool that takes `query`, send `{"query":"..."}`. Read the shape from GET /v1/tools/{name}.

text.description: The tool’s answer as a sentence — what a model would read. Always present.

data.description: The structured result, when the tool produces one; null when its answer is only prose. Its shape is the tool’s own and moves with the tool.

images.description: Present only when the tool returned pictures for a model to look at (view_images, video_frames, a finished image): each as base64 with its mimeType, ready to hand to a vision model.

did_you_mean.description: An argument THIS tool declares that the key most likely meant, or null.

ignored_arguments.description: Present when the call ran WITHOUT keys the tool does not take: each one, with the argument it most likely meant. The text starts with the same news, and data.ignoredArguments carries it too.

ToolJob.description: A handle to a render that is queued or still running, answered with HTTP 202 when `wait` was sent.

status.description: queued or running at the moment of the reply. This enum MAY GROW.

poll.description: The path to poll: /v1/jobs/{id}. Also sent as the `Location` header.

poll_url.description: The same, as an absolute URL.

retry_after_seconds.description: A sensible gap between polls. Also sent as `Retry-After`.

text.description: The tool’s own sentence about the queued render.

type.description: What kind of work it is: video, stitch, avatar, templatead, upscale, and so on. This set MAY GROW.

status.description: queued, running, done or error. `done` and `error` are final. This enum MAY GROW: keep polling on a value you have not seen.

progress.description: 0 to 1, when the worker reports it.

brand_id.description: The profile that started the job.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601. For a finished job, when it finished.

run_at.description: ISO-8601, for work scheduled to start later; null for work that starts immediately.

url.description: The finished file, once `status` is `done` and the job produced one. Always an absolute, publicly reachable URL.

poster_url.description: A still for a finished video, when there is one.

error_message.description: Why it failed, when `status` is `error`. Named `error_message` so it can never be mistaken for this API’s error envelope.

cancelled.description: True when the job was stopped by `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` before it reached a model. Its `status` is `error` and nothing was charged.

result.description: The worker’s full result. PASSTHROUGH TIER: its shape is the job type’s own and improves with it, like a tool’s `data`. Build on the fields above; read this for detail.

outcome.description: `cancelled`: it had not started, it is stopped and nothing was charged. `requested`: it is starting; it stops before it reaches a model if it can, and is charged nothing if it does. `too_late`: it has already reached the model, so it finishes, is charged as usual and lands in the Library. `finished`: it had already ended. This enum MAY GROW.

message.description: A plain sentence for the person who asked to cancel.

running.description: How many of the jobs matching this filter are running right now.

is_default.description: The account’s anchor profile, whose id is the literal `default`. It is what a request with no `X-Hermoso-User` and an unpinned key acts on.

current.description: The profile THIS request resolved to.

shared.description: True for a profile owned by another account that you were invited into.

owner_account_id.description: Only on a shared profile: the value `X-Hermoso-Owner` takes.

role.description: owner for your own profiles; your role on a shared one.

headers.description: Exactly the headers that select this profile.

status.description: This enum MAY GROW — tolerate a member you have not seen.

checkout_url.description: Stripe’s hosted checkout. Present while payment is outstanding. A card is entered there, never here.

expires_at.description: ISO-8601. When the checkout link stops working. Nothing is created and nothing is charged if it lapses.

claim_token.description: Returned ONCE, by the create call. Store it before doing anything else — it is the only proof this signup is yours.

api_key.description: Returned ONCE, on the claim that provisions the account (or on a re-claim inside 24h, which revokes the previous key). Stored only as a hash — it can never be re-read.

email.description: The contact mailbox and its verification state. Present from the create call on.

next.description: What to do now, in one sentence.

note.description: What the state means, in one sentence.

type.description: What to make. This enum MAY GROW.

prompt.description: What the ad should show, in plain words.

model.description: A model id from the live catalog (the `hermoso_capabilities` tool lists them with prices). Omit to let Hermoso pick; the quote then prices the model the server would pick.

aspect_ratio.description: e.g. 1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 16:9. Each model lists the ratios it renders.

image_size.description: Image only: a size tier the model lists (for example 1K, 2K).

duration_seconds.description: Video only: one of the chosen model’s listed lengths.

ref_image.description: Video only: a Hermoso-hosted image to animate (image-to-video).

ref_images.description: Image only: up to 3 Hermoso-hosted images (a `POST /v1/media` or Library `url`) the render uses as its reference. When present the brand’s product photos are not attached for you; the quote prices exactly this.

use_brand.description: Image only, default true: attach the profile’s own product photos (and its logo when the prompt asks for one) so the render shows the real product. The quote prices exactly what this attaches.

format.description: Image only, default png. gif = a short looping animated GIF, svg = an editable vector. Both render on gpt-image-2.6 (default) or gpt-image-2.6-flare from the prompt alone: no ref_images, and the profile’s photos are not attached.

frames.description: format gif only: frames in the loop (default 9).

frame_ms.description: format gif only: milliseconds per frame, rounded to 10 (default 200).

complexity.description: gpt-image-2.6 models only: how much the model plans before drawing (default high). No separate charge.

background.description: Image only: transparent = a PNG with no background (an alpha channel), for a cut-out product, icon or sticker. Renders on gpt-image-2.6 (default) or gpt-image-2.6-flare from the prompt alone: no ref_images, and the profile’s photos are not attached. Priced like a plain image of that size (the quote shows it).

credits.description: What the render reserves. null when it would not start (see `refused`).

likely_credits.description: Present when the hold covers an optional step (a label repair) that usually does not run: the likely charge, `credits` being the most it can be.

label.description: The model or pipeline that will render it.

refused.description: Why the render would not start. Nothing was charged.

reference_images.description: Image only: the pictures the render will use, exactly as it attaches them. With `use_brand` on these are the profile’s own saved product photos (up to three) and its logo when the prompt asks for one; empty when none is on file.

reference_note.description: Image only: a sentence about those pictures when there is one to say (a photo left out, a lineup, the logo).

type.description: image = a static ad image to clone; video = a TikTok, Reel, Facebook, X or YouTube link (or a direct video file). This enum MAY GROW.

url.description: The https URL of the ad image (image) or of the post or video file (video).

type.description: clone_image or clone_video. This set MAY GROW.

credits.description: The sum of every step priced in advance (`flat` and `hold` steps, plus `estimate` steps). Steps with `credits: null` are billed on top at their real cost.

refused.description: Why the clone would not start. Nothing was charged.

next.description: What runs it, in one sentence.

step.description: read_layout, render, copy_and_check, plan or render_video. This set MAY GROW.

credits.description: Its price, or null when it is billed at real cost or priced later.

likely_credits.description: For a `hold` that covers an optional step (a label repair): the likely charge.

basis.description: flat, hold, estimate, metered or later. This set MAY GROW.

video.description: The video the person goes into: a public https link to a video file, a TikTok, Reel, Facebook, X or YouTube post link (read once, through one lookup), or a Hermoso file URL (`POST /v1/media`, `GET /v1/library`, a job `url`).

voice.description: Optional. A NEW voice for the new person, keeping the original words and timing: `match` (a voice that fits them), `female`, `male`, or a stock voice name (Aria, Sarah, Charlotte, George, Brian, Charlie). Omit to keep the video's own sound. Never the original speaker's voice or a cloned one.

language.description: Optional. The new person speaks this language instead (for example `Spanish`), with the mouth lip-synced to the new words. `voice` defaults to `match`.

start.description: Optional. Where the recast window starts, in seconds. Default 0.

end.description: Optional. Where it ends, in seconds. Default: the end of the video, up to 60 seconds after `start`. At least 3 seconds.

instruction.description: Optional, in your own words: who in the video is replaced when there are several people ("the man on the left").

dry_run.description: true = return the exact price and the plan, and run nothing.

callback_url.description: Optional https URL to POST the finished job to (the same as the `X-Hermoso-Callback-Url` header).

RecastPerson.description: Who goes into the video. Send exactly ONE of the three.

creator_id.description: A saved creator's id or exact name, or a preset AI creator's id (the `list_creators` tool lists both). A saved photo of a real person needs a paid plan or a credit pack.

image_url.description: A clear photo of the person (https or a Hermoso file URL). A photo of a real person needs a paid plan or a credit pack, and sending it confirms you have their permission; the confirmation is recorded. A portrait Hermoso made from words for this account counts as an AI person on every plan.

describe.description: An AI person made from your words, on every plan: age, hair, style, vibe ("a man in his 40s, short grey hair, navy sweater"). Never a real or famous person by name. The person is made first (priced as its own step) and lands in your Library.

step.description: `person` (making a described AI person) or `recast`. This set MAY GROW.

credits.description: Its price: what the step reserves when it starts (`basis: hold`) or, once it has run, what it was charged (`basis: charged`).

likely_credits.description: When the hold covers an optional leg that usually does not run: the likely charge.

credits.description: The whole price: the sum of `steps`. An estimate: a real call reserves it and is charged its actual cost, usually within a few percent. null when it would not start (see `refused`).

refused.description: Why it would not start. Nothing was charged.

status.description: `quoted` (a dry run), `refused` (a dry run that would not start), or the job's own status once queued: `queued`, `running`, `done`, `error`. This enum MAY GROW.

engine.description: The model that will render it.

window.description: The part of the video that is recast, in seconds.

kind.description: `person`, or `object` when the picture shows no person (it then replaces the video's subject as an object).

post.description:
Invoke a tool with a JSON body of its arguments and get its result. The body IS the argument object — there is no envelope to wrap it in.

UNKNOWN ARGUMENTS are never silently dropped. A key the tool does not declare that looks like a misspelling or synonym of one it does (`pagId`, `platform` for `target`) is refused with `400 invalid_arguments`, and `error.unknown_arguments` lists each one as `{name, did_you_mean}`, the suggestion always being an argument of THIS tool. Any other undeclared key runs the call without it: the result text starts with a line naming it, and the response carries `ignored_arguments: [{name, did_you_mean}]` (the same list is `data.ignoredArguments`). Keys starting with `_` are host metadata and are never named.

The same handler the MCP server and the CLI run, on the same credential, through the same spend gate: a tool that costs credits costs the same credits here, and one that publishes publishes to the same connected account. Send an `Idempotency-Key` on anything that spends or publishes and a retry is safe.

The reply carries BOTH halves of the tool's answer: `text` is the sentence (what an agent reads) and `data` is the structured result (what an integration reads). A tool that refuses answers with an HTTP error in the standard envelope, never a 200 with a failure inside it.

CONTRACT TIER: the envelope here — the route, the auth, the errors, the rate-limit headers, the idempotency semantics — is stable. A tool's own arguments are not frozen: they improve with the tool. Read `GET /v1/tools/{name}` rather than pinning a schema.

parameters.description: The same as the `X-Hermoso-Callback-Url` header, for a client that cannot set headers. Prefer the header: a callback URL is a secret, and query strings are logged. A callback implies `wait=0` unless you send `wait` yourself.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: How long to hold this request while a render finishes. Only tools that render through the job queue are affected: video, avatars, template ads, post-production, and image generation (`generate_image` is queued as an image job whenever `wait` is sent, including `wait=0`). Every other tool answers as it always does. OMIT IT and nothing changes: a render is held for up to 45 seconds and then answered 200 with `data.stillRendering: true` and a `data.jobId`. `wait=0` (or `false`) answers 202 with a job handle the moment the job is queued, which is what a platform with a 30-second step limit wants. `wait=<seconds>` holds at most that long, capped at 45, and answers 202 if the render is not finished by then. Not waiting never changes what a render costs or whether it runs: the job is queued, checked against your balance and billed exactly as it is when you wait. Poll `GET /v1/jobs/{id}`.

parameters.name: X-Hermoso-Callback-Url
parameters.description: An https:// URL to POST the outcome to, for a platform that cannot poll (for example Zapier `z.generateCallbackUrl()`). When the call queued a job, Hermoso POSTs the job resource — exactly what `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` answers — once the job is `done` or `error`, with headers `Hermoso-Event: job.done | job.error` and `Hermoso-Delivery` (also sent as `Idempotency-Key`; drop a repeat). A 2xx ends delivery; a 4xx other than 408, 425 and 429 is final; anything else is retried for about 16 hours. When the call finished inside the request, its response body is POSTed too (`Hermoso-Event: tool.result`). The response header `Hermoso-Callback` says what happened: `registered`, `sent`, `limit-reached` or `not-registered`. Nothing about what runs or what it costs changes: the URL is attached after the job is queued. A refusal is the HTTP error and nothing is POSTed. Must be https on a public host name; a replay with the same `Idempotency-Key` and a new URL adds that URL to the same job.

The new person performs every move, expression and mouth shape of the original, on the same beats and cuts, in the same set and light, and the original sound is kept. A request that would be refused is refused before anything is charged, with a stable `error.code` and a plain sentence: `real_face_needs_paid`, `face_review_blocked`, `ref_unreadable`, `insufficient_credits`.

post.description:
Create a Hermoso account programmatically, with no human at a browser and no existing credential — the one call in this API that needs no key, because the key is what it creates. Returns a Stripe Checkout URL and a one-time `claim_token`.

AN AGENT THAT HOLDS ITS OWN PAYMENT CREDENTIAL (a Shared Payment Token from a Link agent wallet, or any MPP credential) can skip the checkout page entirely: `POST /api/signup/machine-payment` answers HTTP 402, and the paid retry returns the API key in the same response.

AGENTIC SIGNUP REQUIRES A PAID PLAN. Nothing is created here: no account, no credits, no row. An account exists only once Stripe reports the payment completed, at which point `POST /v1/signup/{id}/claim` provisions it and returns your API key. The free plan is not available on this path — it is available to a person signing up at https://app.hermoso.ai.

A card is entered on Stripe’s own hosted page, never here, so the checkout step itself needs a browser: hand `checkout_url` to whoever is paying. `claim_token` is returned exactly once and is the only proof this signup is yours — a checkout session id alone is not enough, because session ids travel in URLs.

post.summary: Claim a paid signup (poll until ready)
post.description:
Poll this until `status` is `ready`. While payment is outstanding it answers `awaiting_payment` and creates nothing. Once Stripe reports the payment completed it provisions the account, applies the plan and its credits, and returns `api_key` — ONCE.

The key is stored only as a hash and can never be re-read. If you lose the response, re-claiming inside 24 hours mints a replacement and revokes the previous key, so a signup never leaves two live credentials behind. After that window there is no self-serve recovery: an agentic account has a synthetic identity and no mailbox to send a link to. Billing is always recoverable regardless — the payer receives Stripe’s receipts and can manage or cancel the subscription from Stripe’s own portal.

post.summary: Create a connect link for your customer
post.description:
A short-lived hosted link that lets someone with NO Hermoso login connect their own account (Facebook and Instagram, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, Pinterest, Threads, Google Business Profile and the ad platforms) to the brand named by `X-Hermoso-User`. Hand `url` to your customer. They see a short page from Hermoso, accept Hermoso’s Terms and Privacy Policy, sign in on the platform’s own consent screen, and land on your `redirect_url` with `connect_status` (success | cancelled | error), `provider`, `brand`, `link_id`, `account`, `error_code` and your `state` added to its query string (a same-named parameter of yours is overwritten).

THE PLATFORM’S CONSENT SCREEN SHOWS HERMOSO’S NAME, because the connection is made with Hermoso’s app on that platform, unless you saved your own app for it (manage_oauth_apps): then it shows yours. WHITE LABEL: the page your customer sees carries your saved welcome screen (name, logo, colours; connect_welcome_screen) when it is on by default or `welcome` is true, and the link opens on your own connect domain once one is active (manage_connect_domains). `external_id` maps your own customer id to this brand, found again with manage_external_ids.

A link connects ONE provider to ONE brand. It can be retried after a cancel until it expires, and is spent once an account connects. Know when it connects from the `account.connected` webhook event (connect a webhook on the brand and include the `connections` group) or by polling GET /v1/connect-links/{id}. Facebook and LinkedIn then need the Pages chosen: call list_connector_accounts and set_connector_accounts through /v1/tools (the link’s creator owns that choice). Accounts that connect with a pasted key (Bluesky, Telegram) are connected with POST /v1/tools/connect_connector instead.
